'''Motoinari Kofun''' (元稲荷古墳) is an ancient Kofun located in {{ill|Kitayama, Mukocho, Muko City, Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府向日市向日町北山}}. It is part of the {{ill|Mukō Hills Kofuns|ja|向日丘陵古墳群}} and has been Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site within the {{ill|Otokuni Kofun Cluster|qid=Q135491395}}.

Its name derives from the Inari shrine once located on the rear mound's summit. The site is part of a group of Kofuns in Mukō Hills, collectively known as the Mukō Hills Kofuns.

== burial ==
The mound features a {{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|zh|豎穴式石室|qid=Q11598499}} in its central rear section. Measuring 5.56 m in length and 1.9 m in height, the chamber demonstrates unique construction techniques and includes clay layers coated with vermilion. Despite historical looting, a few burial burial goods, such as iron weapons and pottery fragments, have been recovered.

== National Historic Site  ==
In 2016, Motoinari Kofun was included in the National Historic Site Historic Site of the {{ill|Otokuni Kofun Cluster|qid=Q135491395}}.<ref name="NationalHistoric Site">{{Cite web|url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html|title=National Historic Sites Database: Otokuni Kofungun|publisher=Historic Site Online}}</ref>

== Related Facilities ==
* {{ill|Kyoto University Museum|en|Kyoto University Museum|qid=Q11374929|lt=Kyoto University Museum}}: Houses and displays burial goods excavated from Motoinari Kofun.
